title: Etale topos point arrows are geometric lifts into the target strict localization
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S$ and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_s\to S$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point], with $\Omega_t,\Omega_s$ algebraically closed. Let $S_{(\bar s)}$ be the inverse limit of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with structural morphism $\rho:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Regard the geometric points as points of the small etale topos [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; arrows are $2$-morphisms defined on direct images [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and their inverse-image mates act on set-valued geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. There is a canonical bijection
$$\Theta:\{a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S_{(\bar s)}\mid \rho a=\bar t\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(\bar t,\bar s).$$
For a lift $a$, the mate of $\Theta(a)$ sends a represented germ $[U,\bar u,z]$ at $\bar s$ to $[U,c_{U,\bar u}a,z]$ at $\bar t$, where $c_{U,\bar u}:S_{(\bar s)}\to U$ is the canonical neighbourhood projection (using affine refinements if $U$ is not affine). For every field automorphism $\tau$ of $\Omega_t$ satisfying $\bar t\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau=\bar t$, changing geometric lifts by $\bar v\mapsto\bar v\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau$ defines an automorphism $r_\tau$ of the point $\bar t$, and
$$\Theta(a\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau)=\Theta(a)\circ r_\tau.$$
No normality, Noetherian, finite-type, support-specialization, or algebraicity-of-$\Omega_t$ hypothesis is required.

proof.text: For each etale S-scheme U, put H_U=(h_U)^#, and write theta:h_U -> H_U for the sheafification unit. The representable-stalk bijection identifies (h_U)_x with lifts x -> U, sending the class of a map f at (V,v) to fv, naturally in U. The sheafification-stalk bijection transports this identification to (H_U)_x. Thus a lift u:x -> U corresponds to the distinguished germ e_u=[U,u,theta_U(id_U)]. These identifications are natural for S-maps of etale schemes: H_f sends e_u to e_(fu). Here x can be either geometric point, and there is no restriction on the extension defining x.

proof.text: Use the small representative category J_s of affine pointed neighbourhoods in the definition of S_(s). Its inverse-limit projections c_(V,v) are compatible. For a possibly nonaffine pointed (U,u), choose an affine pointed refinement f:(V,v) -> (U,u) and set c_(U,u)=f c_(V,v), transporting through a representative of J_s if necessary. This is independent of the choice: cofilteredness supplies a common pointed refinement, equalizes the two maps into U if necessary, and affine initiality supplies a further affine refinement. On it both composites agree by the cone identities. The same argument gives compatibility with every pointed neighbourhood morphism. Each c_(U,u) is over S since rho is the composite of any affine projection with its structure map.

source.place: Tag 0GJ2, section-specialization: germ construction; converse and equivariance proved here from representable stalks, Yoneda and the defining inverse limit.

proof.text: Given a:Spec Omega_t -> S_(s) over S, set v_(U,u)=c_(U,u)a, using the compatible projections of step 2. This assigns (U,v_(U,u)) to (U,u) and preserves every pointed refinement, since f c_(V,v)=c_(U,u) for a pointed f:(V,v)->(U,u). The maps F(U) -> F_t, z |-> [U,v_(U,u),z], consequently form a compatible cocone for the colimit defining F_s. They induce lambda_a:F_s -> F_t with precisely the stated formula, independently of representatives. A sheaf morphism sends z to its image and commutes with restrictions, so these maps are natural in F. The inverse-image/direct-image adjunction mate correspondence defines a unique 2-morphism Theta(a):t -> s with mate lambda_a. This also establishes the formula on nonaffine U without requiring F(U) to be represented on an affine U in any unique way.

source.place: Tag 0GJ2, section-specialization: germ construction; converse and equivariance proved here from representable stalks, Yoneda and the defining inverse limit.

proof.text: Conversely, let alpha:t -> s have inverse-image mate lambda:F_s -> F_t. For each affine pointed (U,u) in J_s apply lambda_(H_U) to e_u from step 1; its image corresponds to a unique lift v_(U,u):Spec Omega_t -> U over S. If f:(V,v)->(U,u) is pointed, naturality with respect to H_f and the identity H_f(e_v)=e_u give f v_(V,v)=v_(U,u). Thus these lifts are a cone on the defining small inverse-limit diagram. Its universal property gives a unique a_alpha:Spec Omega_t -> S_(s) with c_(U,u)a_alpha=v_(U,u). Composing any projection with U -> S shows rho a_alpha=t. This construction uses no specialization assumption or extension of an embedding between the two geometric fields.

source.place: Tag 0GJ2, section-specialization: germ construction; converse and equivariance proved here from representable stalks, Yoneda and the defining inverse limit.

proof.text: We check the two constructions are inverse. Starting with a, step 3 sends e_u to e_(c_(U,u)a); step 1 therefore recovers exactly the projections c_(U,u)a, and inverse-limit uniqueness recovers a. Starting with alpha, take any germ [U,u,z] of a sheaf F at s. By affine cofinality it suffices to take U affine. Yoneda gives the presheaf map h_U -> F associated to z; the sheafification universal property factors it uniquely through q_z:H_U -> F. On stalks q_z sends e_u to [U,u,z] and e_w to [U,w,z]: this follows by evaluating the Yoneda map on id_U and then restricting. Naturality of lambda with q_z now gives lambda_F([U,u,z])=[U,v_(U,u),z]. This is the mate of Theta(a_alpha) by step 3. Every germ has such a representative, hence the mates agree on every sheaf, and the mate correspondence gives Theta(a_alpha)=alpha. The construction and its inverse involve only canonical maps, so the bijection is canonical.

source.place: Tag 0GJ2, section-specialization: germ construction; converse and equivariance proved here from representable stalks, Yoneda and the defining inverse limit.

proof.text: Let tau be a field automorphism fixing t as a scheme map. On F_t define R_tau[U,v,z]=[U,v Spec(tau),z]. Pointed refinements remain pointed after this change of lifts, so the stalk-colimit relations are respected, and the formula commutes with sheaf morphisms. Replacing tau by its inverse gives an inverse natural transformation. Taking mates therefore defines the point automorphism r_tau:t -> t. For every germ [U,u,z] at s one has lambda_(a Spec(tau))([U,u,z])=[U,(c_(U,u)a) Spec(tau),z]=R_tau(lambda_a([U,u,z])). Thus lambda_(a Spec(tau))=R_tau lambda_a. Inverse-image mates reverse the direction and order of direct-image transformations: the mate of Theta(a) composed with r_tau is exactly R_tau lambda_a. By uniqueness of mates this proves Theta(a Spec(tau))=Theta(a) composed with r_tau. Only the equality t Spec(tau)=t was used.
